A cold damp seeps in through the gaps between the wall planks. There is no one to bear witness to your vow...
From above the Bay of Revachol, a cold wind gathers in response. The people of the fishing village pull their coats and blankets tight about themselves...

And ever and ever... Out of the corner of your eye, you see the hair on the back of your hand standing on end. It feels as though low-grade lightning is coursing through you. You must be hypersensitive from the hangover.
Something is on its way. Something hidden. It's coming, a miracle -- from the northwest -- and it's almost here. You can feel it in the air on your hands, the cold spring air smoothing them over.

Behind this building -- the other one. Once filled with engineers and designers of Feld Electric, now collapsed and dead, but for some rats... You feel drawn, for some reason, to the faded mural again.
The snow falls on her shoulders, then melts in her light blond hair... Cold and soft.
The rain falls on her shoulders, tinting her blond hair light brown. It smells of industrial pollution and brine.
A squall of seagulls under the low-hanging sky. Distant machinery from the harbour. It's wide open and cold.
The wet wind, heavy with brine and industrial pollution from the stacks nearby, ruffles her hair.
Between here and Jamrock, a dusty sea of old trees, all covered in industrial soot. Small houses under them, an overgrown park...
The hair on your arms stands up... electricity. Sounds like reeds hissing.
This is the smell of dying reeds, of longing crumbling into the water.
High above and to the east, the cold winds blow over the feathers of an early songbird. She lands on the stone ledge of a tall building. Her beak a silvery grey.
Long shadows, short shadows. Quiet shadows of local children, loud shadows drunks and also a shadow made of sticks... you breathe on your hands for warmth.

On Clinton Street, near the Boogie Street Diamond, a small truck rattles down an alleyway. It stops by a rusted trash container. Two men, their faces rough and swollen, jump out. They look at the container, despondently. CSM is written on their backs...
An almost unbearable tension fills the room. The hairs of your back stand up.

A tremble comes over you, another after-effect of ethanol poisoning perhaps? Feels like leaves do when they rustle in the breeze, somewhere far away, below the Turbine. The 41st and the 57th... The lieutenant was right. It's not about who gets what's North, it's about who doesn't.
Heavy drops of rain fall on the colliding eyebrows and run down the worn faces. The world outside this stand-off almost doesn't exist.
Snowflakes fall and immediately melt in the heat of the colliding eyebrows. Nothing exists outside this moment.
It's as if the entire world is frozen solid in awe of this great clash of brows. Nothing exists outside this moment.
Sheets of rain over the water. A flight of stairs leading into the ocean. Wave after wave washing the coast of Martinaise, with its motorboats and gently swaying reeds.
The rain falls.
A yard. Rain falls onto the roof of a woodshed. The lingering odour of decomposition mixes with that of damp soil.
Looking up at the sky, cold water dripping from your hair.

A traffic jam. Rain thrumming on the roofs of motor vehicles. Inside, drivers watch water streaming down their windshields. The statue of a king shudders, he too is cold. The canal bridge has been raised.
No. You are just one of the hundreds of thousands who watch them rise across the bay from Martinaise every day.
Two green snakeskin shoes stand at attention on the mosaic paving of the plaza.
Standing in the rain, looking north, where Jamrock Rock City stretches inland.
The great gates of the industrial harbour are locked. A chill runs down your back. You shudder like an animal trying to shake water from its hide.
A yard. Rain falls onto the roof of a woodshed. Coal leaks into a puddle beneath a dead man's feet. He swings from a tree, bloated. Droplets of rain slip from his cold cheeks.
Your hair sticks to your forehead, cold and wet.
To be in Martinaise, where no one goes. At the run-off point of a long-forgotten canal, in the whitest part of town. In the shadow of the day the Revolution failed.
In the rain-swept distance above the rooftops of Jamrock, a re-purposed silk mill stands perched above the motorway exit. Precinct 41 hunches in the rain.
Your shirt sticks to your chest. The shoulders of your disco blazer grow heavy. The cold finds its way in under your skin. You shiver, and the city shivers with you.
Hallways collapsed from the mortar hits of a war that was lost long ago. Clotheslines go to waste in the rain. Radios play.
More coalition aerostatics. Way up there -- where rain forms -- rotors flutter silently. Your sight clears.
You shudder, looking down at your feet. Dirty rainwater runs veins into the plaza snow.
A silvery curtain of rain over the houses. The class divide.

Urban coastline, rain dripping off eternite-covered roofs. Cinder blocks left over from half-finished construction. A defunct research and development building once seized by revolutionaries. An old wooden church stands on stilts above the water.
The skyscrapers of La Delta, the financial district. Faint golden light seeps from the office windows.
Humid. Your coat shields you from the rain while the city shivers around you.
Coalition aerostatics hang like apparitions under the cloud cover. Way up there -- where rain forms -- rotors flutter silently. Your sight clears.
Capeside apartments -- tower blocks crowd one another, 4.46 mm bullets still lodged in their war-torn stone walls.
You realize you have no shoes on. Your feet are red with cold.
Your shirt sticks to your chest. The shoulders of your jacket grow heavy. The cold finds its way under your skin. You shiver, and the city shivers with you.

These spring thaw will not last. The winter will return to Revachol.
YOU CANNOT RETURN.
HAVE A BROTHER IN THE CUT. WHERE THE WOOD AT?
Winter's grip on the city is loosening. The spring thaw is here.
Grey sky like great battleships, clouds colliding with one another. Rain falls down on the world.

Collapsed storm drains. Old sewage systems flooded with rainwater. Hidden weapon caches from the Revolution. Doors leading down to Le Royaume -- the catacombs to which, for three centuries, they delivered the blue-blooded dead.
The shoulders of your jacket grow heavy. The cold finds its way under your skin. You shiver, and the city shivers with you.
Water runs down your bare chest. The cold finds its way under your skin. You shiver, and the city shivers with you.
Revachol is the capital of the world. Jamrock is the capital of Revachol. Droplets form on your eyelashes.

Behind the gates -- heaps of supply crates. Red and blue metal shipping containers slick with rain. The Greater Revachol Industrial Harbour is an artificial mountain range. Immense wealth resides within, and immeasurable poverty in its shadow.
Coal City, end of all lines.

On a street there that flows like a muddy river in the snow, with fire traps rising on either side. A film rental opens its doors to the rain, an armoured motor carriage rushes past the corner where you used to walk together... Suddenly, the hair on your back rises.
The ruins of a half-sunken seafort crumble on an inlet. Beyond the Bay of Revachol, ghosts rise into the sky.
Your hair is an oily mess flecked with ash from neighbouring coal plants. Smoke stacks rise somewhere in the distance.
All around you, rain falls on the great city of Revachol. Rain drips from the eaves and floods the gutters, washing the filth away.
Couron, the lower middle class. Distributary after distributary cuts the city blocks in half. Seven-story buildings trail off into the rain.

The road ascends; a raised motorway loops above the ghetto. Beneath its concrete columns -- a sea of rooftops, woodwork, and tar stretches northward. Four-story buildings as far as the rain can fall. The snows melt in Jamrock.
La Drisienne, King Dris's Passenger Harbour. Cruise ships flanked by dock arms. Cranes watching over the mouth of the river distributary.
Your vision blurs. You wipe your face with your hand. The rain stings your eyes, making you look up and blink.
The spring thaw must be here. The snow is melting...
You -- on the Martinaise plaza. A small dot looking up at the sky. Droplets form on your eyelashes.
You realize you still have only one shoe. Nearby, on the balcony of the Whirling-in-Rags hostel-cafeteria, a single crocodile-skin shoe now fills with rainwater.
And then suddenly you see it: over all the other graffitos someone has -- using the tip of a very sharp knife -- cut the words: REVACHOL FOREVER.
The building is tall, seven stories wind-wrapped in solitude; most of the apartments are unoccupied. This was a suicide. The other an accident -- the small one.
A small green enclosure in the middle of a corral of tenements: Capeside Apartments, Whirling-in-Rags and the fortress wall of Terminal B. Above it -- a thin blanket of coastal stratus clouds.
YOU WERE.
Higher yet, Coalition airships guard over the twenty one cordons of the Zone of Control. The air is criss-crossed with radio transmissions, the hair on your neck rises...
A column of cold air encircles you, rising slowly upward in the shape of a courtyard; bordered by cracked plaster, windows, seagulls perched on air conditioning units.

A drop of sweat runs down your nose and in it you see the Martinaise inlet, wrapped in the night. In the abandoned fish market two figures face each other in a spectacular light-show. One of them is forced to stare into the three empty barrels of a gun. Not an uncommon sight in the neighbourhood.

A drop of sweat runs down your nose and in it you see the Martinaise inlet, wrapped in the night. In the abandoned fish market three figures stand in a spectacular light-show. A large, loud woman is pointing an empty firearm at the other two. She doesn't want to listen... or even to be heard.
The wind howls over the Bay of Revachol -- a cascade of cold air, flowing through the tangled city streets.

You haven't heard a word of what she's been saying these past few moments. You only hear...
Remorse. The parquet of assembly halls, the rows of stall bars are growing cold. The corridors stand empty. A girl's voice somehow finds its way through this strange feeling...
The gale wind blows in from the coast, a wind of needles. It wraps itself around a building of brick and mortar. Somewhere, a clamor rings through the honeycomb of classrooms.
THERE IS A HOLE IN MY HEART.

High above, the wind wraps the church in its rush. Cold and wet from the ocean bay, it parts around the massive keel-shaped roof. Like a test tunnel washing both sides, the way it has done for three-hundred-and-forty years. The wind keeps its distance. So should you.
Feels like electricity and a very small piece of nothingness.
YOU ARE IN ITS ARMS.
There is a hawthorn tree on Rue de Saint-Ghislaine, right next to the canal. A reel of magnetic tape is caught in its branches, like bronze ribbons blowing in the wind...
THE WORLD IS A COLD SINK.
The skin on your back is crawling. For a second you can't even hear the music anymore.

The wind brings some snow in from the broken gallery. It wraps you in its embrace, cold and luminous. You should return to the mural soon, to the one that said: Tomorrow is just a whisper away.
So many walls all over Martinaise -- weatherworn, cracked, their paint peeling...
A slight sensation of static electricity, as before a storm. A miniature conference is taking place inside, and you are the subject.
Has it gotten cold in here? Your arms seem to be covered in gooseflesh.
A low pressure system is gathering itself over the bay. It's begun to tug violently at the tarpaulins...
Now the breeze has subsided. All is still except for the last bits of steam rising from the coffee pot.
A cold wind whips at the canvas. From far below, the sounds of waves smashing themselves against the rocks. You are exposed.

In a nearly forgotten part of that glorified construction site, surrounded by rusted pieces of scaffolding and walls of faded tarpaulin, a detective of the RCM debates the intricacies of an abstruse theory with a pair of university students...
The attitude of a priest bearing one of the holy relics of his faith. Though it is long out-of-service, its power is evident to him.
Somehow you only now realise that the temperature has been dropping steadily for the last half hour.
THIS IS YOUR CITY. DEFEND IT AT ALL COSTS.
Air moving through what was once a row of apartments protected by walls and a roof. It sighs through the remains of bedrooms and parlours...
A soft rustling. The snow seems to have gotten between your ears somehow...
DON'T FORSAKE ME, OFFICER. I AM YOUR RESPONSIBILITY JUST AS YOU ARE MINE.

There is something, a whisper, circulating among the city's footnoted alleyways and along its electrical wires, but what it's saying, you can't tell. It seems to be a message meant for someone else...
A slight frisson at the point where your neck meets your spine. Something about the lieutenant's words, directed at you, but not *you*...
You are the Doom-Speaker. It is your lot to ply these somnolent roads, declaring your lonely truth...
A soft rustling. Between your ears, a winterscape with fast falling snow...
Every lightswitch, every motor carriage, every doorbell, tea kettle, and radio in Martinaise, all mingled with electrical interference caused by scattered thunderstorms over Ozonne.
Le Jardin, Stella Maris, Saint-Batiste. She is looking down on the suburbs of Revachol East.
... the old and irregular streets, like a grid drawn by a palsied hand. The open fires burning in oil drums, visible through blasted roofs...

Slowly peeled by the wind... Your skin crawls from the sensation as you look around.

Wind rips through the empty hallways of the once great military hospital, now just a ruin under an overgrown park. Beneath the hospital, great sewer tunnels hum and vibrate with life of their own...
Despite the cold, figures move about cloaked in shadow, their breath escaping in white clouds that fade into the darkness. Wherever you look, the night gives cover to her messengers.
